clue.text: Book, one passed on to descendants by relative

blocks.note: a gene is the unit of heredity handed down through generations
short for sister, a family member

explanation.surface: A family heirloom, perhaps a book, handed down to the descendants by a relation.
explanation.definitionFit: The first book of the Old Testament, telling of the creation of the world.

clue.text: Mock exam's beginning after major upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down clue flips the word end to end
beginning points to just the opening letter of exam being used

blocks.note: major means big, here read backwards
first letter of exam

explanation.surface: A student taunted when an exam starts after a big upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To gibe is to jeer or taunt someone, the same as to mock them.

clue.text: Bigwig — why he eats off his lap?

definitions.text: why he eats off his lap?

blocks.note: first meaning: an important person

blocks.clueFragment: why he eats off his lap?
blocks.note: second meaning, read cryptically: he has nothing to put his plate on

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TABLE, the answer explains a plate balanced on knees.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable is a person of distinction or importance, just as a bigwig is.

clue.text: No bath for Solomon's mother before state visit from here?

indicators.note: No tells us to strip a word away, here the word bath

blocks.note: Bathsheba was King David's wife and mother of Solomon
taken as written: the word to be taken away

explanation.surface: Biblical gossip: Solomon's mother skipped her bath before a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bathsheba was famously seen bathing by David; remove BATH. The Queen of Sheba made a celebrated visit to Solomon's court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba travelled from her kingdom to visit King Solomon, a biblical state visit.

clue.text: Stuff for treating water succeeded with greater regularity

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
more often

explanation.surface: A water treatment that works more reliably than before.
explanation.definitionFit: A water softener is a substance or device that removes hardness minerals from water.

clue.text: Man about to fail to take catch, for example

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the man's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: a man's name, read backwards
to miss something is to fail to take it

explanation.surface: A fielder fumbles a catch, the classic cricket blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a dropped catch, but in cricket a catch is one way to send a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a catch is one method by which a bowler or fielder gets a batsman out, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Old satirist is boring to study

blocks.note: something dry is dull and boring
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A complaint that an old satirical writer is tedious to read.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden, the 17th-century poet, wrote satires such as Absalom and Achitophel.

clue.text: Test of opinion gets desperate measure cut

blocks.note: a drowning person clutches at a straw, a desperate last resort
to poll is to cut or crop hair or horns

explanation.surface: An opinion survey prompts a desperate step to be axed.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal vote taken to gauge general feeling.

clue.text: Popular part of the Bible? Just the opposite

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: Asking whether a well-loved Bible passage says the reverse of what we think.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means opposite or reversed in order or effect, the contrary of something.

clue.text: Sort of electronics firm, say

blocks.note: solid and firm both mean hard and stable
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A company in the electronics trade, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company noun, but it is the adjective meaning hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid-state electronics use semiconductors such as transistors rather than valves.

clue.text: Insect flew pointlessly into food store

indicators.note: without points: the compass-point letters in the word flew are dropped
into means the shortened word is placed inside the food store

blocks.note: a buttery is a pantry or storeroom for provisions
taken as written, then losing the compass points E and W

explanation.surface: A fly zooms aimlessly into the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: E and W are compass points, so 'pointlessly' strips both from flew. A buttery is an old word for a pantry, still used in colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly is a winged insect with broad, often colourful wings.

clue.text: Show, not a delightful entertainment

indicators.note: not a tells us to remove one letter A from the word for show

blocks.note: to reveal is to show

explanation.surface: A grumble that some show was no fun at all.
explanation.walkthrough: REVEAL loses its A to give REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively, merry festivity or celebration enjoyed by a crowd.

clue.text: Apocalyptic future vision warrior's given to his continent

blocks.note: a brave is a Native American warrior; the 's is read as 'is'
the Americas, home continent of such a warrior

explanation.surface: A grim prophecy of a warrior handing over his land.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's novel imagines a dystopian future society, so it is a bleak futuristic vision.

clue.text: Winning hand producing sign the king's embarrassed?

blocks.note: first meaning: the best possible poker hand
second meaning, read whimsically: a monarch reddening in the face

explanation.surface: A card player blushes at holding an unbeatable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a flush on a royal face.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the top hand is ace to ten of one suit; read literally it is a reddening of royalty.

clue.text: In summary, have finished struggle with wife

blocks.note: when something is over it has finished
to vie is to compete or struggle
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A brief account of someone ending a battle alongside his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An overview is a general outline, a brief survey of the main points.

clue.text: See strange tree on hillside showing lots of spiny segments

indicators.note: strange means odd or unfamiliar, so the letters appear in an unusual order

blocks.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see
the letters to be rearranged
brae is Scottish for a hillside

explanation.surface: Look at an odd tree on a slope, with many spiky parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertebrae are the bones that link together to form the backbone or spine.

clue.text: Compelling dope to stay in bed

indicators.note: to stay in something is to be inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
dope and gen are both slang for information

explanation.surface: A dazed or drugged person forced to remain in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs or a fool, but here it means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is persuasive and convincing, which is what compelling means.

clue.text: Getting down overheads in court? Excellent!

blocks.note: first meaning: hitting overhead shots hard down in tennis
second meaning: an exclamation of approval

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court where overheads are smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a smash is a hard overhead shot; informally, smashing means splendid or excellent.

clue.text: Notice animal's accommodated on Ark, for example

indicators.note: accommodated means housed, so one piece is lodged inside another

blocks.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a boar is an animal; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sign announcing that an animal has been given a berth on Noah's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship such as Noah's Ark means on board the vessel, as a passenger would be.

clue.text: Works collected in No. 10. perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: a volume gathering several works
second meaning: a bus route number

explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 suggests Downing Street, but here it is a bus route.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition collects several works in one volume; an omnibus is also the full name for a bus.

clue.text: Writer's block restricting girl

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a sett is a stone paving block
a moll is a girl, especially a gangster's companion

explanation.surface: Writer's block holding an author back from a woman character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the definition is Writer's, and block gives the stone. Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett was a novelist, author of Roderick Random and Humphry Clinker.

clue.text: Four expelled from government and put to death

indicators.note: expelled from means thrown out, so those letters are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: Roman numeral for four
the executive is the governing branch

explanation.surface: Four ministers thrown out of the cabinet and then killed.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the Roman IV from EXECUTIVE leaves EXECUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute someone is to carry out a death sentence on them.

clue.text: Largely mysterious success for naturalist

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: dark means obscure or mysterious
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A puzzling triumph for a nature scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: DARK minus its last letter gives DAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the Victorian naturalist who proposed evolution by natural selection.

clue.text: Seen fawning revoltingly round a king, Ulysses successor

indicators.note: revoltingly suggests rising in revolt, so these letters are overturned and rearranged
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the extra pieces

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Courtiers seen fawning repulsively around a monarch, Odysseus's heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses looks like the Greek hero, but it is James Joyce's novel; the answer was his next and last.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce wrote this novel after Ulysses, so it followed that book in his output.

clue.text: Part in theatre needed in kitchen-sink work?

blocks.note: first meaning: the stage area in front of the curtain
second meaning: a garment worn while washing up

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen-sink drama is gritty realist theatre, so the surface stays in the playhouse while the second meaning is literal washing up.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is both the forward stage area in a playhouse and a protective garment for kitchen chores.

clue.text: Pyramidologist reveals pagan statue

indicators.note: reveals means lets us see what is inside the long word

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: An Egypt scholar uncovers a heathen figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or figure worshipped as a god.

clue.text: River commonly said to be dark brown

indicators.note: commonly said means spoken in a dropped-aitch Cockney way, so the opening letter H is lost

blocks.note: the Humber is an estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: The water of a river described, in local speech, as murky brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is a river estuary in Yorkshire and Lincolnshire; a Cockney drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brownish colour.

clue.text: Party organiser has circular for collection

blocks.note: a whip enforces discipline within a political party
round and circular both describe a ring shape

explanation.surface: Someone arranging a party sends out a leaflet asking for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip is the parliamentary official who keeps a party's members voting together.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal gathering of money from a group, for a gift or cause.

clue.text: Banshee possibly could do for one declining

indicators.note: possibly hints at one possible arrangement of the letters rather than the given order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wailing Irish spirit might well finish off someone in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or success is past and fading.

clue.text: Well-bred set capturing record? Almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter of the word for record goes
capturing means holding inside, so the word for set surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does
to enter data is to record it; then cut short

explanation.surface: A refined crowd nearly grabbing some prize or record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun for a social group, matching Well-bred, but it is the verb meaning solidify.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel describes refined, polite manners associated with good upbringing.
